task.title: Inspect one finite recurrence by exact ID
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/871 by exposing exact read-only recurrence lookup without scanning unrelated streams.
acceptance_criteria: Validate the caller-supplied recurrence ID before storage access and replay only its exact owning stream.
Emit the established complete deterministic recurrence JSON shape for a found definition.
Fail closed for missing storage, absent identity, or malformed exact evidence while ignoring unrelated corruption and preserving read-only authority.

attempts.diagnostic: The focused CLI integration test failed because recurrence get was not recognized.
attempts.patch: Added exact success, invalid identity, missing database, absent recurrence, malformed selected stream, unrelated corruption, and non-mutation coverage.

attempts.diagnostic: Inventory filtering would perform unrelated work and let unrelated corrupt streams block a caller-selected lookup.
attempts.patch: Added recurrence get using typed identity validation and RecurrenceStore::load, reused recurrence JSON projection, categorized failures, and ADR-0043.

attempts.summary: Recorded the exact-head review limitation and merge disposition.
attempts.diagnostic: The initial CodeRabbit run was rate limited; its later exact-head no-actionable-comments summary also reported 14 UNAVAILABLE: Connection dropped, so the review evidence was inconclusive.
attempts.patch: Kept auto-merge disabled through the cooldown and shared-budget checks; after exact-head Rust success, the no-actionable summary yielded no findings or follow-ups, and the merge authority accepted the remaining review limitation.

outcome.summary: The CLI retrieves one exact finite recurrence deterministically without scanning unrelated streams or mutating the selected database.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- record validate corpus/development/0169-exact-recurrence-lookup-cli.json # result: valid development record
nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- corpus inspect corpus/development # result: inspected 171 records: 171 valid, 0 invalid

lessons: Exact lookup should address one owning stream instead of filtering a full inventory.
Validate identity before touching storage so invalid input cannot create or inspect a database.
Unrelated corruption must not block a caller-selected exact read.

The exact-head CodeRabbit summary reported both no actionable comments and a connection-dropped tool failure; auto-merge remained disabled through cooldown and verification checks, but the run was inconclusive and supplied no findings or follow-ups.
Successful local verification does not waive substantive exact-head review.
